questions.q: What is the relationship between contour line spacing and slope steepness on a topographical map?
questions.a: Closely spaced contour lines indicate a steep slope, while widely spaced contour lines indicate a gentle slope. A wrong answer (e.g., saying wide spacing means steep) reveals the student has not grasped the inverse relationship between horizontal equivalent and gradient.

questions.q: Why does a concave slope show contour lines that are closely spaced at the top and widely spaced at the bottom?
questions.a: A concave slope is steeper at the top and gentler at the bottom; since steepness is shown by close contour spacing, the top has closely spaced contours and the bottom has widely spaced contours. A wrong answer (e.g., reversing the pattern) indicates confusion between concave and convex slope profiles.

questions.q: On a 1:50,000 topographical map with a contour interval of 20 m, you measure the horizontal distance between two adjacent contours on a slope as 2 mm on the map. Calculate the average gradient of that slope in degrees (use tan θ = vertical interval / horizontal equivalent). Is the slope gentle or steep?
questions.a: Horizontal equivalent = 2 mm × 50,000 = 100,000 mm = 100 m. Vertical interval = 20 m. tan θ = 20/100 = 0.2 → θ ≈ 11.3°. Since gradient < 15°, it is a gentle slope. A wrong calculation (e.g., forgetting to convert map distance to ground distance) reveals inability to apply scale and contour interval together.

questions.q: Compare the slope patterns on the windward and leeward sides of a hill in the Western Ghats as shown on a topographical map. How would the contour spacing differ and what does it indicate about erosion processes?
questions.a: The windward side (facing rain-bearing winds) typically shows steeper, more closely spaced contours due to higher erosion, while the leeward side shows gentler, widely spaced contours. A student who cannot differentiate sides or link to erosion reveals a lack of analytical connection between physical processes and map representation.

questions.q: A student claims that on a topographical map, a convex slope is always steeper than a concave slope. Evaluate this statement with reference to contour patterns.
questions.a: The statement is false. Convex and concave refer to the shape of the slope profile, not absolute steepness. A convex slope can be gentle overall (widely spaced contours at top, closely spaced at bottom) while a concave slope can be steep overall (closely spaced at top, widely spaced at bottom). The claim confuses slope shape with slope gradient. A wrong evaluation shows inability to distinguish between gradient and profile curvature.

questions.q: Sketch a cross-section profile from a given contour map segment (contours at 100m, 120m, 140m, 160m, 180m with increasing spacing from top to bottom) and annotate it to show the slope type. Propose a suitable land use for this slope in the context of Indian agriculture.
questions.a: The increasing spacing from top to bottom indicates a convex slope. Suitable land use: terraced farming or plantation crops (tea, coffee) on the upper gentle part, with soil conservation measures on the steeper lower part. A poor answer would misidentify the slope type or suggest inappropriate land use (e.g., intensive cultivation on steep lower slopes without conservation).

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Contour ______ for slope types involves analyzing the spacing and arrangement of contour lines on a topographical map to classify terrain steepness and profile shape: gentle slopes show widely spaced contours, steep slopes show closely spaced contours, concave slopes display contours that are closely spaced at the top and widely spaced at the bottom, while convex slopes show the opposite pattern (widely spaced at the top, closely spaced at the bottom).
Fill in the blank: Imagine trekking in the ______ Ghats near Munnar: some trails are easy while others are exhaustingly steep.
What must you be able to do to master this topic?
questions.a: Can correctly identify gentle, steep, concave, and convex slopes on a Survey of India 1:50,000 topographical map by analyzing contour spacing and pattern, and can explain the quantitative relationship between contour interval, horizontal equivalent, and slope gradient.

questions.q: Fill in the blank: Imagine trekking in the Western Ghats near Munnar: some trails are easy while others are ______ steep.
